ob-stronger.alt: Valid order block checklist: the move broke structure (BOS), left a fair value gap, the zone is unmitigated, and it agrees with the higher-timeframe trend
ob-stronger.caption: A stronger order block ticks all four boxes: break of structure, an imbalance (FVG), unmitigated, and in line with the higher timeframe.

ob-trading.alt: How to trade an order block: wait for price to return to the zone, confirm with a lower-timeframe change of character, stop loss beyond the order block, target the next liquidity
ob-trading.caption: Trading an order block: wait for the return, confirm on a lower timeframe, place the stop beyond the zone and target the next liquidity.

ob-vs-sd.h2: Order block vs supply and demand
ob-vs-sd.alt: Order block vs supply and demand zone on the same chart: the order block is one candle and tighter, the demand zone covers the whole base and is wider
ob-vs-sd.caption: The same move marked two ways: an order block uses one candle, a supply and demand zone covers the whole base.

bos-close.alt: Break of structure: a candle body closing beyond the swing high is a real BOS; a wick that pokes through and closes back inside is a liquidity sweep
bos-close.caption: Count a break when the candle body closes beyond the level. A wick through and a close back inside is usually a liquidity sweep.

bos-internal.alt: Internal vs swing structure: inside a higher-timeframe uptrend the pullback makes its own internal CHoCH, which only ends the pullback before the swing high breaks
bos-internal.caption: Swing structure is the big highs and lows. An internal CHoCH inside the pullback often only marks the end of the pullback, not a reversal.

fvg-test.alt: Fair value gap test results: a limit entry at the 50% consequent encroachment level won 31% of trades at 1:2 versus 28% for random zones over 23,773 FVGs on Gold and EURUSD
fvg-test.caption: Our test of 23,773 FVGs: a limit order at the 50% level (CE) beat random zones of the same size in 8 of 8 tests; a plain touch-and-bounce did not.

fvg-plan.alt: How to trade a fair value gap: higher-timeframe direction, an FVG left by the move that broke structure, entry on the return into the gap, stop beyond it and target the next liquidity
fvg-plan.caption: An FVG plan in four steps: direction first, the gap left by the break of structure, the return into it, then stop and target.

liq-where.alt: Where liquidity sits on a forex chart: buy stops above equal highs and the previous day high, sell stops below equal lows and under a trendline
liq-where.caption: Liquidity pools: above equal highs and the previous day's high, below equal lows and along trendlines that many traders draw.

liq-stop.alt: Stop loss placement and liquidity: a stop exactly at the obvious low gets swept, a stop with a buffer below the level survives the sweep
liq-stop.caption: Do not place your stop exactly at the obvious level. Give it a buffer so a liquidity sweep does not take you out.

smc-pd.alt: Premium and discount in SMC: the range from swing low to swing high split at the 50% equilibrium, with the OTE optimal trade entry zone at 62–79% of the retracement
smc-pd.caption: Above 50% of the swing is premium, below is discount. OTE is the deep 62–79% part of the pullback; combine it with an order block or FVG.

smc-kz.alt: ICT killzones in Pakistan time (winter): London killzone about 12–3 PM PKT and New York killzone about 5–8 PM PKT, after the Asian range
smc-kz.caption: Killzones are the busy hours when sweeps and displacement happen most: about 12–3 PM and 5–8 PM PKT in winter.

pa-candles.h2: 1. Candles: what each bar tells you
pa-candles.alt: Reading candlesticks in price action: a big bullish body, a long lower wick, a pin bar at support and a bullish engulfing candle
pa-candles.caption: What each candle says: the body shows who won, the wick shows rejection, a pin bar at a level and an engulfing candle show a shift.

pa-mtf.alt: Multiple timeframe analysis in price action: H4 gives the trend and level, H1 shows the pullback to the level, M15 gives the engulfing entry with a tight stop
pa-mtf.caption: Top-down: the higher timeframe gives direction and levels, the middle timeframe the setup, the lower timeframe the entry candle.

pa-triggers.alt: Four price action entry triggers at a level: rejection wick, engulfing candle, breakout and retest, and false breakout
pa-triggers.caption: Four entry triggers at a level: rejection, engulfing, breakout and retest, false breakout. Act only after the candle closes.

sb-setup.h2: What the Silver Bullet setup is
sb-setup.alt: ICT Silver Bullet setup inside the one-hour window: a sweep of a nearby high, displacement with a market structure shift, entry in the fair value gap, stop beyond the sweep
sb-setup.caption: Inside the hour: a sweep of nearby liquidity, a strong move the other way with a structure shift, then an entry in the FVG it leaves.

sb-markets.alt: Which ICT Silver Bullet window to trade from Pakistan: London 1–2 PM for EURUSD, GBPUSD and Gold; New York AM 8–9 PM for Gold and US indices; New York PM 12–1 AM
sb-markets.caption: Which window suits which market: London for EURUSD, GBPUSD and Gold; New York AM for Gold and US indices; New York PM is quieter.
